newsitem.title: USA: Biogen says Berlex suit dismissed.
newsitem.headline: Biogen says Berlex suit dismissed.

text.p: Biopharmaceutical company Biogen Inc said on Tuesday a U.S. District Court dismissed a suit filed by Berlex Laboratories Inc claiming the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's approval of its AVONEX product was improper.

Judge James Robertson held the FDA acted lawfully when it determined that AVONEX, an Interferon beta-1a, was "clinically superior" to Berlex's Betaseron under the U.S. Orphan Drug law and that "FDA's determination that AVONEX is safe, pure and potent is amply supported by the record," Biogen said.
Berlex, a subsidiary of Schering AG, had filed the suit against the FDA and Biogen said it joined with the FDA to fight it.
Berlex was not immediately available for comment.

Biogen said AVONEX, used to fight multiple sclerosis symptoms, was the only drug shown to slow the growth of physical disability. The company said its product only needed to be taken once a week and had moderate side-effects.

Jim Vincent, Biogen chairman and chief executive officer said: "This is a major victory for the multiple sclerosis community and Biogen. The Berlex action was frivolous and inappropriate and against the best interests of people with MS and their physicians."
